analysis.title: Last Man Standing
key_insights: Mag7 is the last cohort of SPX-important stocks that has not shown weakness, up about 1% on the day, and it is the most widely owned group because of its perceived safety against rates and geopolitical risk. A reversal in Mag7 is what BTIG expects would cause sustained SPX weakness.
Prior-day SPY volume was the lowest for a non-holiday session since 2003. Volume and volatility are somewhat higher on the day of the note.
Semis remain a weak link. If the 2000 analog holds, SOX should bottom within 24 hours, get one final rally, then sell off more sharply later in October.
The SOX 2000 analog timing coincides with the next day's CPI, which BTIG notes can act as a catalyst.

The IGV/SMH ratio is above its 200 DMA for the first time in 16 months. A move above the summer high of .20 would confirm a major inflection, with software likely to outperform semis over the coming months.
XLU has rallied 7% off its lows 13 trading days after closing with RSI below 22, which triggered BTIG's bullish tactical call. BTIG would take profits and look for a reset.

ITB fell 2% over two days while IYR rose 2%, an unusual split for normally correlated groups. Since 2006 there were only two prior instances, and ITB rose 13% over the next 17 days after 4/2/07 and 11% over the next 3 days after 5/24/22.
BTIG does not like the early pop and fade in homebuilders but keeps a bullish tactical bias as long as ITB holds above about $83.

The S&P 500 Oil & Gas Refining Index is up about 13% since BTIG's cautious call a month ago, and BTIG acknowledges it was wrong so far. With the index 63% above its 200 DMA, BTIG still expects extreme downside reversion over the coming weeks and months.

sector_views.rationale: SOX tracks the 2000 analog, with a short-term low expected, one last rally, then an accelerating selloff later in October.
IGV/SMH ratio is above its 200 DMA for the first time in 16 months and software is expected to outperform semis.
XLU is up 7% from its lows after the tactical bullish call, so BTIG would take profits and look for a reset.
Rare divergence with REITs has historically preceded gains in ITB. The bullish tactical bias holds while ITB stays above about $83.
The index is 63% above its 200 DMA after a roughly 13% rise in a month, and BTIG expects a harder snap-back.
